implementation_notes: C has no objects, so the query descriptor is a struct that owns the statement text and a parallel value array, composed by free functions (query_where/query_and) with explicit ownership rules; the interpreter is the SQLite C API - sqlite3_prepare_v2 compiles the text, sqlite3_bind_* attaches the values, sqlite3_step executes and sqlite3_finalize releases. What replaces the classic object graph is the struct plus a naming convention (and a function-pointer table when predicates must be polymorphic); the hand-written form stays justified when the query shape is fixed enough that a static prepared statement needs no composition at all.
pitfalls: Splicing values into the fragment text defeats the pattern: keep values in the parameter array and bind them with sqlite3_bind_*.
Every early exit must still reach sqlite3_finalize; a leaked statement keeps the database locked and the fragment struct hides the leak.
A sqlite3_stmt is not re-entrant (one per thread at a time), and SQLITE_STATIC versus SQLITE_TRANSIENT decides whether the bound buffer must outlive the step.
